title: Sreekariyam Abhiram murder: Death by double strangulation, SIT formed
content: The Keralam Police on Tuesday formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to probe the murder of A D Abhiram, a 17-year-old boy whose body was found stuffed in a sack and dumped in a plantain farm near a temple in Pangappara in Thiruvananthapuram. The SIT has been constituted under the supervision of the Deputy Commissioner of Police (Law and Order), Thiruvananthapuram City. It comprises the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Cyber City, two police inspectors, cyber investigation and forensic experts, and other officers. One person, a female named Anantha, has been arrested. Two others, the prime accused (A1), a minor, and the second accused, Umar Muftar S (A2), a history sheeter, have been remanded in custody. Anantha is A3, the third accused. Her name was revealed by City Police Commissioner Dr Arul R B Krishna, as she is not a minor. The police investigation has found that Anantha's mobile was used by A1 to communicate with the victim in the days preceding the crime, and also to lure the victim to the spot of the crime. The police believe that Anantha was a willing accomplice. "The first accused used the Instagram ID of A3 (Anantha) to summon the victim to a pre-arranged spot. It has also been found that A1 had chatted with the victim disguised as A3 in the days before the murder. So A3 was fully aware of what was going on," the Police Commissioner said. The third accused has knowledge of the crime, but whether her involvement runs deeper will be revealed only during the investigation. According to the police, the first accused was infuriated by the closeness of his former lover with the friend of Abhiram, the victim. Abhiram, in short, was not the target but was sought to be used as a tool to somehow get his friend to the crime spot. Further, the investigation has revealed that the crime was committed together by A1 and A2. "The minor and Umar participated equally in the crime," the Commissioner said. In fact, Umar was at the spot when the victim arrived, lurking in a corner where there were no cameras. "The findings of the doctor during the postmortem were suggestive of strangulation," the Commissioner said. The police suspect that the first and second accused had strangled the victim alternately, one by using his hands and the other by tightening a belt around the neck. Umar was picked up for questioning after the call records of the prime accused were checked. Already, Sreekaryam police records showed that the prime accused was the second accused in three theft cases in which Umar was the first accused. So picking up Umar, after finding that he had been called by the prime accused, was a logical step. The Commissioner said that the two accused had also entered into what he called a "strategic deal". "If at all they were caught, it was decided that they would say that the murder was committed by the first accused. This way Umar would be spared and the minor would receive only a lenient sentence under the Juvenile Justice Act," the Commissioner said. He said that the two accused stuck to their plan till noon on Tuesday but eventually confessed to the crime. Initially, it was thought that Abhiram, a native of Pangappara, was strangled with a belt by the minor and that he then sought the help of Umar to dispose of the body. The boy was reported missing at Sreekariyam Police Station on the morning of November 2. A missing-person case was initially registered under Section 57 of the Kerala Police Act, 2011. During the investigation, the police gathered evidence pointing to a murder, following which Section 103(1) (murder) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, was added to the case. The second accused, Umar Muftar S, is a resident of Puthen Veedu, Puthuvval, Kallampally, Sreekariyam. He is a rowdy history-sheeter and a KAAPA accused with several criminal cases against him. He was released from preventive detention under KAAPA on September 1...
